title: Move Axum auth into a middleware
summary: Put auth in one place with from_fn_with_state, then split out /health with route_layer and merge after .layer locks it.

turns.user: stop calling authenticate in me and orders every time. make it a middleware. handlers should still get the user

assistant.body: Let's pull auth into one place! middleware::from_fn_with_state wraps the routes in require_auth, which puts the CurrentUser it finds into the request extensions. Handlers just take Extension<CurrentUser>, a clean separation of concerns.

turns.user: deployed and /health returns 401 now, k8s liveness keeps killing pods. also unknown URLs give 401 instead of 404

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was wrong. .layer wraps every route registered before it and the fallback too, so /health and any unknown path went through require_auth. Moving /health below .layer would also fix it, but a setup that depends on line order breaks easily. Instead, the routes that need auth go into their own Router with route_layer, and merge joins it back. route_layer only runs when a route matches, so unknown paths still answer 404.

turns.user: oh sorry the token comes in an x-api-key header, not Authorization. no Bearer prefix either

assistant.body: Got it. The header name changes and the line that strips Bearer goes. The header import is no longer used, so the same sed removes it and no warning is left.
